description: The self-explaining check exempts Markdown, JSON and JSONL files, including plans/ and executions/ records, because their prose is not code. Nothing verifies that the exemption does not let code fences in those files become the only place explanatory prose or commented code lands.
goal: Verify and pin the exemption: add tests that run scripts/check_self_explaining.py on real temporary git repositories showing that a Markdown file under plans/ or executions/ containing a fenced code block with a docstring and comments passes, and that the same text in a Python file fails, and make the check also fail a changed Markdown file under plans/ or executions/ whose fenced Python, shell or YAML block adds a docstring or a comment that is not a '# why:' reason, if the verification shows such blocks pass unchecked today. Ledger JSONL files stay exempt. Code is self-explaining: no docstrings and no comments except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.
rationale: An exemption that is not tested can become the loophole through which the rule is broken.
acceptance_criteria: The Markdown ledger and plan exemption is verified: a test in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_self_explaining_markdown_coverage.py runs scripts/check_self_explaining.py on a real temporary git repository whose diff adds a Markdown file under plans/ with a fenced Python block holding a docstring and a plain comment, and asserts the documented outcome (fail if fenced code is checked, otherwise an assertion pinning that it passes with the reason).
The same test file asserts a Markdown prose paragraph and a JSONL ledger row added in the diff never fail the check.
The same test file asserts the same docstring in an added Python file fails.
scripts/self_explaining_comments.py classifies fenced code in Markdown consistently with the verification test and its existing behaviour for source files is unchanged.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest' and 'uv run task lint' passes.
